question: When do critical hits add and refresh Fluff of Ferocity stacks?
decision: Use the shared post-hit ProcCallback phase: each connected critical packet/target adds one stack, capped at ten, and resets the whole stack group's ten-second deadline even at cap. The triggering hit and other hits already queued at that timestamp use prior stacks. Keep wearer-only stacks off-field. This event order and per-packet/per-target multiplicity are explicit tested hypotheses.
availability: Frozen Global release availability remains unverified.
stop_condition: Check T1-T5, independent critical-damage arithmetic, no-crit/zero/dead-target cases, ten-stack cap and refresh, expiry before equal-time hits, wearer ownership and CLI/WASM/Worker parity.
return_condition: New trigger multiplicity, callback order, clock, off-field or release evidence conflicts with the model.
checks: 146 content tests pass: exact T1-T5 parameter ratios and units; critical-only triggers, zero/dead-target delivery, simultaneous-hit ordering, ten-stack cap, refresh at cap, exact expiry, off-field ownership and invalid configurations.
Independent oracle: 1000 ATK * .5 DEF * (2 + prior stacks * .04) gives 1000, 1020, 1040, 1060, 1080, 1100; ten stacks give 1200. A capped trigger refreshes all stacks through the next deadline.

Public Baicang A0 level 80 purchased talents 8/8/8 with compatible equipped T1-T5 weapon runs three skills, checks CRIT damage multiplier (1 + native CD + stack bonus)/(1 + native CD), expiry and fixed noncritical mode. This partial action model does not claim a complete Baicang kit.
TypeScript, production studio build, weapon passive Worker tests, native_build and scenario_script modules pass. Full CLI/WASM report parity is checked with NTESIM_VERIFY_NATIVE=1.
Content clippy passes with only the two pre-existing metadata lints collapsible_if and single_element_loop allowed. Changed Rust files are formatted; frozen source bytes are preserved.
